input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Dashboard run comparison view (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

Delivers a comparison surface in the Dashboard where users select two or more
training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side,
including a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics
changed between two selected runs. This replaces the current workflow in which
comparison happens only in exported spreadsheets because parameters and
metrics are confined to per-run pages.

## Scope

- Multi-selection of two or more runs from the existing runs list, covering
  both training runs and pipeline runs.
- A comparison view presenting each selected run's parameters and metrics side
  by side.
- A diff presentation over the same comparison data that highlights which
  parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs (a presentation
  mode of the comparison surface, not a separate view family).
- Read-only comparison; data sourced from the same per-run parameters and
  metrics the existing run detail pages show.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list, when the user selects two or more runs and opens the
  comparison, then each selected run's parameters and metrics are displayed
  side by side in the Dashboard.
- Given two selected runs in the comparison, when the diff presentation is
  chosen, then the parameters and metrics that differ between the two runs are
  highlighted.
- The comparison works for pipeline runs using the run data already surfaced
  by the platform's pipeline capabilities, and for training runs.
- Given fewer than two selected runs, the comparison action is unavailable or
  prompts for more selections.
- No regression to the existing per-run detail pages.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): select two or more runs and view parameters and metrics side by
  side in the Dashboard — primary scope of this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): run diff view highlighting changed parameters and metrics —
  bundled here as a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the
  same run data; covered at the higher of the two priorities (P0). The
  strategy notes the two requirements' wording overlaps because they were
  consolidated from two customer councils; they are one capability.

# Model version run lineage in the Model Registry

## Description

Registered model versions record a link back to the run that produced them,
so the producing run is identifiable from the Model Registry. This is the
registry-side half of enabling a comparison to be opened from the Model
Registry.

## Scope

- Store a reference to the producing run on registered model versions, using
  the registry's existing metadata extension point for structured model
  version metadata.
- Expose the run reference on the model version through the registry's REST
  API so platform surfaces (such as the Dashboard) can read it.
- The reference must identify the run within its project so it can be
  resolved back to a specific training or pipeline run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a known producing run, when the run
  reference is recorded, then it is retrievable through the model registry
  REST API.
- Given the run reference, the producing run is resolvable to a specific run
  in its project.
- Given a model version with no run reference, the version remains valid and
  the absent reference is handled gracefully by API consumers.
- Recording the run reference is backward compatible with existing model
  versions and registry clients.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them — registry-side storage and exposure of the run reference.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

From the Model Registry UI in the Dashboard, users can open the run
comparison for the run linked to a registered model version, so promotion
decisions can start from the registry rather than only from the runs list.

## Scope

- In the model version detail view, surface the producing run recorded on the
  model version.
- Provide an action that opens the run comparison view with the linked run
  included, allowing further runs to be added to the comparison.
- Apply to both training and pipeline runs linked from model versions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a linked producing run, when the user
  opens the comparison from the Model Registry, then the Dashboard comparison
  view opens with that run included and further runs can be added.
- Given a model version without a linked run, the comparison entry point is
  absent or disabled without breaking the model version detail view.
- The opened comparison presents parameters and metrics and the diff between
  runs consistent with the runs-list-driven comparison experience.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" — the
  Dashboard-side entry point that consumes the run reference stored on model
  versions and the run comparison capability.

# Pipeline-run comparison data validation

## Description

Validation, owned by the Data Science Pipelines team, that pipeline-run
parameters and metrics are accessible and complete enough for side-by-side
comparison and diff as consumed by the Dashboard. Data Science Pipelines is a
passive component in this strategy — no code changes are anticipated, because
pipeline runs and their details are already surfaced through the platform's
existing pipeline capabilities; this epic validates that assumption for the
comparison use case and is owned by a different team than the Dashboard
implementation.

## Scope

- Enumerate the parameters and metrics exposed for pipeline runs through the
  existing pipeline run surfaces the Dashboard consumes.
- Validate retrievability, naming consistency, and completeness of that data
  for side-by-side comparison and diff of two or more runs.
- Produce a validation report; any gap is documented with its impact on run
  comparison and handed to the Dashboard comparison work as a remediation
  input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering pipeline-run parameter and metric
  exposure for the comparison use case.
- Every check in the report has an explicit pass/fail result.
- Any identified gap is documented with concrete impact on side-by-side
  comparison or diff and communicated to the Dashboard comparison work as a
  remediation item.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): supports side-by-side comparison of pipeline runs — validation
  of a passive component (no code changes) owned by a different team than the
  implementing epic, delivered as a separate validation epic.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

Product documentation covering the run comparison workflow from both entry
points: the runs list and the Model Registry.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and using the diff highlighting
  between two runs.
- Comparing runs from the Model Registry: following a registered model
  version's producing-run link and opening the comparison from there.
- Coverage of both training runs and pipeline runs in the comparison
  workflow.
- Placement within the existing Dashboard and Model Registry documentation
  sets, with cross-links from the per-run and model version documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics cover the comparison workflow from the runs list and
  from the Model Registry, including the diff presentation.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the
  comparison view, the model version run reference, and the registry
  comparison entry point.
- The topics are published in the product documentation set with working
  cross-links.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.
